 148 people sickened by unknown G.I. outbreak aboard Caribbean Princess cruise ship 
 The cruise ship departed from Ft. Lauderdale, Florida, on Nov. 11 for a 12-night cruise to the Caribbean, Colombia and Panama Canal. 
 By Danielle Abreu • 
 Published November 18, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 18, 2026 at 1:24 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Joe Raedle/Getty Images 
 The Princess Cruises’ Caribbean Princess is seen docked at Port Everglades on March 12, 2020 in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. 
 An outbreak of a gastrointestinal illness has sickened nearly 150 passengers and crew members aboard Princess Cruise ship currently on a voyage in the Caribbean, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. 
 The Caribbean Princess departed from Ft. Lauderdale, Florida, on Nov. 11 for a 12-night cruise to the Caribbean, Colombia and Panama Canal, according to the cruise's itinerary.

 The outbreak was first reported to the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program on Saturday. So far, 134 of the ship's 2,936 passengers and 14 of 1,132 crew members have reported being sick, according to the CDC, which added that not all the infected people were sick at the same time. 
 The agency said the cause of the outbreak is not yet known, but the main symptoms among those who fell ill were diarrhea and vomiting.
 In response to the outbreak, the crew aboard the ship has increased cleaning and disinfecting procedures, collected stool specimens for testing, and isolated the sick passengers and crew members, according to the CDC. 
 In a statement to NBC, a spokesperson for Princess Cruises confirmed an outbreak described as a "mild gastrointestinal illness."
 "While most guests remain unaffected, we are continuing to closely monitor the situation," the spokesperson said, adding the ship remains on its scheduled voyage and is scheduled to return to Florida on Nov. 23.

 It marks the fourth outbreak of an illness aboard a Princess cruise ship this year, according to the CDC, the most of any cruise line. In March, 153 people aboard the Star Princess were sickened by a norovirus outbreak during a Caribbean cruise and two months later in May, another 160 passengers and crew members were sickened by norovirus during another Princess Caribbean cruise, the CDC reported. In July, more than 120 passengers and crew members on Ruby Princess were stricken by norovirus while on a voyage to Canada and Alaska.
